```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)

library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
library(readr)

# Project root: edit to your own directory
base_dir <- dirname(dirname(normalizePath(knitr::current_input())))

source(file.path(base_dir, "code", "apa_helpers.R"))

tab_dir <- file.path(base_dir, "code", "apa_output", "tables", "maia")
fig_dir <- file.path(base_dir, "code", "apa_output", "figures", "maia")
```

# Purpose

Exploratory check of whether trait interoceptive awareness (the eight MAIA-2
subscales) is associated with the drawing outcomes. Each subscale is added as a
predictor in a separate model, on top of the pre-registered structure:

$$\text{outcome}_z \sim \text{timepoint} \times \text{group} + \text{MAIA\_subscale} + (1 \mid \text{PID})$$

Outcomes are z-scored within study; MAIA subscales are z-scored within study, so
the reported coefficient is the expected change in the outcome (in SD units) per
1 SD of the subscale. MAIA-2 is trait-level and constant within a participant, so
this is a between-person association.

# Load and prepare

```{r prepare}
df1 <- read_csv(file.path(base_dir, "data", "processed", "interomap_study1_data.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
df2 <- read_csv(file.path(base_dir, "data", "processed", "interomap_study2_data.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

maia_subscales <- c(
  "Noticing"              = "MAIA_Noticing",
  "Not-Distracting"       = "MAIA_NotDistract",
  "Not-Worrying"          = "MAIA_NotWorry",
  "Attention Regulation"  = "MAIA_AttnReg",
  "Emotional Awareness"   = "MAIA_EmoAware",
  "Self-Regulation"       = "MAIA_SelfReg",
  "Body Listening"        = "MAIA_BodyListen",
  "Trusting"              = "MAIA_Trusting"
)

# Z-score outcomes and MAIA subscales within study.
prepare <- function(df) {
  df |>
    mutate(
      # z-scored outcomes
      avg_valence_z             = as.numeric(scale(avg_valence_combined)),
      avg_intensity_z           = as.numeric(scale(avg_intensity_combined)),
      extent_log_z              = as.numeric(scale(log(extent_combined + 1))),
      valence_by_extent_log_z   = as.numeric(scale(log(valence_by_extent_combined + 1))),
      intensity_by_extent_log_z = as.numeric(scale(log(intensity_by_extent_combined + 1))),
      centroid_x_front_z        = as.numeric(scale(centroid_x_front)),
      centroid_y_front_z        = as.numeric(scale(centroid_y_front)),
      sd_x_front_z              = as.numeric(scale(sd_x_front)),
      sd_y_front_z              = as.numeric(scale(sd_y_front)),
      entropy_15_front_z        = as.numeric(scale(entropy_15_front)),
      # z-scored MAIA subscales
      across(all_of(unname(maia_subscales)), ~ as.numeric(scale(.x))),
      timepoint = factor(timepoint, levels = c("pre", "post")),
      group     = factor(group, levels = c("non_gambler", "gambler")),
      PID       = factor(PID)
    )
}

df1 <- prepare(df1)
df2 <- prepare(df2)

study1_outcomes <- c(
  "Valence"                    = "avg_valence_z",
  "Intensity"                  = "avg_intensity_z",
  "Extent (log)"               = "extent_log_z",
  "Valence x Extent (log)"     = "valence_by_extent_log_z",
  "Intensity x Extent (log)"   = "intensity_by_extent_log_z",
  "Centroid x"                 = "centroid_x_front_z",
  "Centroid y"                 = "centroid_y_front_z",
  "SD x"                       = "sd_x_front_z",
  "SD y"                       = "sd_y_front_z",
  "Entropy (15)"               = "entropy_15_front_z"
)

study2_outcomes <- c(
  "Valence"      = "avg_valence_z",
  "Centroid y"   = "centroid_y_front_z",
  "SD x"         = "sd_x_front_z",
  "Entropy (15)" = "entropy_15_front_z"
)
```

# Fit models

```{r fit-models}
# lmer with Satterthwaite df; returns only the MAIA subscale coefficient.
fit_maia <- function(df, outcome_col, sub_col) {
  f <- as.formula(paste(outcome_col, "~ timepoint * group +", sub_col, "+ (1 | PID)"))
  s <- summary(lmer(f, data = df, REML = TRUE))$coefficients
  s[sub_col, , drop = FALSE]
}

run_study <- function(df, outcomes) {
  lapply(names(outcomes), function(onm) {
    dv <- outcomes[[onm]]
    lapply(names(maia_subscales), function(snm) {
      r <- fit_maia(df, dv, maia_subscales[[snm]])
      data.frame(
        outcome  = onm,
        subscale = snm,
        estimate = r[1, "Estimate"],
        se       = r[1, "Std. Error"],
        df       = r[1, "df"],
        t        = r[1, "t value"],
        p        = r[1, "Pr(>|t|)"],
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    }) |>
      bind_rows()
  }) |>
    bind_rows()
}

res1 <- run_study(df1, study1_outcomes) |> mutate(study = "Study 1")
res2 <- run_study(df2, study2_outcomes) |> mutate(study = "Study 2")

results <- bind_rows(res1, res2) |>
  mutate(
    subscale = factor(subscale, levels = rev(names(maia_subscales))),
    ci_lo = estimate - 1.96 * se,   # Wald 95% CI for the forest plot
    ci_hi = estimate + 1.96 * se
  )

# APA-formatted table view (subscales in questionnaire order, Noticing first).
maia_apa_table <- function(dat) {
  dat |>
    mutate(
      subscale = factor(subscale, levels = rev(levels(subscale))),
      b        = round(estimate, 2),
      SE       = round(se, 2),
      df       = round(df, 1),
      t        = round(t, 2),
      p        = fmt_p(p),
      `95% CI` = sprintf("[%.2f, %.2f]", ci_lo, ci_hi)
    ) |>
    arrange(outcome, subscale) |>
    select(Outcome = outcome, Subscale = subscale, b, SE, df, t, p, `95% CI`)
}
```

# Results

## Study 1

```{r table-study1, results='asis'}
s1_tab <- maia_apa_table(filter(results, study == "Study 1"))

cat(apa_tab_caption("MAIA Subscale Fixed Effects \u2014 Study 1 (Outcome and Subscale z-Scored)"), "\n")
apa_table(s1_tab, "maia_study1", tab_dir)
cat("\n*Note.* b = standardised coefficient (outcome SD per 1 SD of subscale); Wald 95% CI; df = Satterthwaite degrees of freedom. Models also include timepoint, group and their interaction (not shown).\n")
```

```{r forest-study1, fig.width=12, fig.height=14}
f1 <- results |>
  filter(study == "Study 1") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = estimate, y = subscale, xmin = ci_lo, xmax = ci_hi)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_pointrange() +
  facet_wrap(~ outcome, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "Standardised coefficient (outcome SD per MAIA SD)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()

apa_fig(f1, "maia_forest_study1", fig_dir, width = 12, height = 14)
f1
cat("\n", apa_fig_caption("Standardised association of each MAIA-2 subscale with each outcome \u2014 Study 1"), "\n")
```

## Study 2

```{r table-study2, results='asis'}
s2_tab <- maia_apa_table(filter(results, study == "Study 2"))

cat(apa_tab_caption("MAIA Subscale Fixed Effects \u2014 Study 2 (Outcome and Subscale z-Scored)"), "\n")
apa_table(s2_tab, "maia_study2", tab_dir)

```

```{r forest-study2, fig.width=12, fig.height=8}
f2 <- results |>
  filter(study == "Study 2") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = estimate, y = subscale, xmin = ci_lo, xmax = ci_hi)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_pointrange() +
  facet_wrap(~ outcome, scales = "free_x") +

```

# Interpretation

`b` is the MAIA subscale fixed effect from `lmerTest::lmer` (Satterthwaite
degrees of freedom). The remaining terms (`timepoint`, `group`, their interaction)
are in every model but are not reported here; see the Study 1 and Study 2 reports
for those. These are exploratory models, not corrected for multiple comparisons.
